title: ha/dr: automate multi-AZ failover + restore drills (terraform/helm/installer + runbooks-as-code)
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in regulated environments require repeatable, testable HA and DR automation for multi-AZ deployments. Previously we relied on ad-hoc runbooks and manual Terraform/Helm steps which made scheduled restore drills and emergency failover brittle. This PR adds automated multi-AZ failover and restore drills, Helm chart improvements to support pod topologySpread and zone-aware affinity, Terraform module changes for cross-AZ state handling, an installer hook to perform safe upgrades/rollbacks, and runbooks-as-code to codify drills and postmortem steps.

What changed (high level):
- Terraform: new module redwood_ha_az supporting multi-AZ load-balancer failover, EBS/GCE persistent volume replication guidance via module outputs, and safer state migration helpers (plan-only migration job).
- Helm charts: add topologySpreadConstraints, podAntiAffinity refinements, probe tuning for N+1 failover, and values to opt into zone-local persistent volumes. Charts include helm unit tests and haproxy ingress tweaks for active/passive routing.
- Private installer: add pre-upgrade validation hook that checks KV cache replication lag and a post-upgrade verification script to run restore drills automatically in CI. Also add upgrade/rollback helper scripts that capture and snapshot critical state before applying changes.
- Runbooks-as-code: new directory docs/runbooks/ha-dr with markdown runbooks and a single-file executable playbook (bash+python) that can be used by SREs to run a restore drill end-to-end. Runbooks include expected metrics, SLO checks, and rollback play triggers.
- CI: add e2e restore-drill workflow that runs against a staging multi-AZ cluster (test infra) and gates merge if it fails. Improvements to terraform fmt/lint checks and helm linting.
- Tests: integration tests for failover path, synthetic traffic generator for soak testing, and new unit tests for the terraform helpers.

Backwards compatibility: changes are opt-in via Helm values and Terraform module flags. Existing single-AZ installs are unaffected unless customers explicitly enable multi-AZ mode.

Rollout plan: we will roll this to staging for 2 weeks of soak. Customer-facing docs will be published in the private-installer repo docs site and a guidance post will be created for dedicated customers.

Related: ENG-2019 (HA initiative), INF-1776 (DR automation spike), pr-42186 (previous runbooks baseline).
